item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of the Environment published a draft ministerial ordinance for public comment on 2026-11-20 to amend the ordinance amending the Enforcement Regulations of the Water Pollution Control Act and related provisions. The supporting material concerns review of the electroplating industry's interim hexavalent chromium effluent limit of 0.5 mg/L, applicable through 2027-03-31, compared with the general limit of 0.2 mg/L effective from 2024-04-01. It reports that 50 establishments exceeded the general limit in fiscal 2025 while meeting the interim limit, with unresolved treatment and reoxidation issues. The excerpts do not establish the proposed replacement limit or extension period; they describe planned promulgation within fiscal 2026 and planned commencement on 2027-04-01. item.title: Draft banking ordinance, capital adequacy notice and supervisory guideline amendments
item.description: AI summary: The Financial Services Agency announced draft amendments on 2026-11-18 for public comment to the Regulation for Enforcement of the Banking Act, prudential notices and supervisory guidelines, allowing consolidation of subsidiary funds in proportion to ownership interests. The proposals would establish Pillar 3 disclosure provisions and notifications and forms for starting or suspending proportional consolidation, and clarify that leverage, liquidity and total loss-absorbing capacity (TLAC) rules use the same consolidation scope as capital adequacy calculations. They would also update domestic-standard banks' disclosure forms for items whose transitional measures have expired and adjust provisions defining internationally active banks in notices applicable to bank holding companies. Similar amendments are planned for specified non-bank financial institutions. The supplied excerpts do not establish a comment deadline or commencement date. item.title: Draft Cabinet Order amending rules on mobile subscriber identification and misuse prevention
item.description: AI summary: The draft Cabinet Order would expand the offenses listed under Article 8(1)(ii) of the mobile subscriber identification law to include specified unauthorized-access and criminal-proceeds offenses, and extend another existing offense entry. It would also update statutory references in the offense-designation order, the whistleblower-protection implementing order and the National Police Agency Organization Order, reflecting the removal of 'voice' from the mobile communications law's title. These amendments accompany the implementing Act No. 25 of 2026 amending the Act on Identification of Subscribers by Mobile Voice Communications Carriers and Prevention of Improper Use of Mobile Voice Communications Services (Act No. 31 of 2005). The draft specifies commencement on 2027-04-01, the stated commencement date of the amending Act. The public-comment notice was published on 2026-11-20, with a stated deadline of 2026-12-21 23:59 JST; the listed authorities are the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications and the National Police Agency. item.description: AI summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications announced this draft Cabinet Order consultation on 2026-11-19, with a stated consultation period of 2026-11-20 to 2026-12-21 and a listed deadline of 2026-12-21 23:59 JST. item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-19, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare published an announcement that the Tokyo Labour Bureau had issued a worker-dispatch business improvement order against Medical World Co., Ltd. under Article 49(1) of the Worker Dispatching Act. The bureau found that, from at least 2024-10-01 through 2025-06-27, the company conducted dispatch operations totaling 362 person-days for duties covered by Article 2(1)(vii) of the Act's Enforcement Order without a statutory exception, violating Article 4(1) of the Act. The visible portion of the order requires a comprehensive review of all worker-dispatch, contracting and secondment operations for violations of the Worker Dispatching Act and the Employment Security Act. item.title: MLIT announces review of Keisei Electric Railway's proposed passenger fare-cap changes
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-19, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism announced that the Transport Council had begun reviewing Keisei Electric Railway Co., Ltd.'s application to change railway passenger fare caps, following a ministerial referral dated 2026-11-18. The application proposes average fares paid increasing by 14.1% overall: 14.3% for ordinary fares and 13.7% for season tickets, comprising a 16.9% increase for commuter tickets and an 11.5% decrease for student tickets. These comparisons include the existing railway-station accessibility surcharge, which the application proposes abolishing alongside the fare revision. A public hearing under Article 23 of the Act for Establishment of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism is planned in Tokyo in January 2027, with the exact date, venue and participation procedures to be announced separately. This is an application under review, not an approved fare change; the excerpts do not state an implementation date.
